item.case_name: A one-minute explainer with a fixed sequence of facts: the citric acid cycle
item.title: Citric acid cycle, a 60 s explainer

turns.text: Make a 60-second widescreen explainer video on the citric acid cycle (the Krebs cycle) for first-year biology students. Show the cycle as a loop inside a mitochondrion: acetyl-CoA enters and joins oxaloacetate to form citrate, two carbons leave as CO2, NADH, FADH2 and ATP are produced along the way, and oxaloacetate is regenerated so the loop starts again. Label the key molecules on screen as they appear, under the title 'Citric acid cycle'. Calm English narration explaining each step as it happens. Simple clean 2D animation, no music.

item.tests: Tests a one-minute explainer with a fixed order of facts: whether the system keeps one consistent diagram across a minute, letters short labels correctly, narrates the steps in order, and stays within the length.

answer_sheet.Style: simple clean 2D animation, a diagram-like loop inside a mitochondrion; your call on colours
answer_sheet.Narration: calm English narration, your wording, as long as the steps are explained in order
answer_sheet.Labels: the key molecules named on screen as they appear, under the title 'Citric acid cycle'

must_haves: The cycle is shown as a loop, as a simple clean 2D animation inside a mitochondrion, not live action.
The steps appear in order: acetyl-CoA joins oxaloacetate to form citrate; two carbons leave as CO2; NADH, FADH2 and ATP are produced; oxaloacetate is regenerated.
Calm English narration is audible and explains each step as it happens.
The key molecules are labelled on screen as they appear, and the title 'Citric acid cycle' is shown.

stages.text:
Citric acid cycle
kind: explainer
style: 60-second widescreen explainer in simple, clean 2D animation using textbook-style diagrams; calm English narration; no music.
Under “Citric acid cycle,” an oval mitochondrial cutaway shows a symbolic, arrow-linked loop in the matrix. Labels identify molecules as calm English narration follows the reactions. Acetyl-CoA supplies a two-carbon acetyl group to four-carbon oxaloacetate, forming six-carbon citrate; CoA-SH is released.

Citrate rearranges into six-carbon isocitrate. Isocitrate becomes five-carbon α-ketoglutarate: CO₂ leaves and the first NADH appears. Next, four-carbon succinyl-CoA forms, releasing a second CO₂ and producing a second NADH. The departing carbons are not the newly arrived acetyl carbons.

Succinyl-CoA becomes succinate, releasing CoA-SH; a GTP → ATP callout represents one ATP equivalent, not two additional products. Membrane-embedded succinate dehydrogenase converts succinate to fumarate as FAD becomes FADH₂. Water enters as fumarate becomes malate.

Malate becomes oxaloacetate, producing the third NADH. The regenerated oxaloacetate can accept another acetyl group, closing the loop. The completed turn shows two CO₂, three NADH, one FADH₂ and one ATP equivalent.
stages.note: research: Citric acid cycle — research for one complete turn inside a mitochondrion, rather than a historical discovery episode. Follow acetyl-group entry, energy capture, carbon dioxide release and oxaloacetate regeneration. Dates below identify source publication dates, not dates when these recurring biochemical reactions occurred. The 60-second running time is a presentation choice, not the measured duration of one turn.

items.prompt: A clean 16:9 textbook diagram designed for legibility at 480p. White background, flat pastel fills, navy outlines, no gradients. Across the top, the exact title "Citric acid cycle" in large navy lettering. Below, a broad peach mitochondrial cutaway with two membranes and sparse folded cristae around its edges; the pale cream matrix contains a large clockwise pathway loop. The pathway is clearly a symbolic diagram, not a physical circular organelle structure. Eight pale rectangular molecule panels surround the loop: "Oxaloacetate" at upper left, "Citrate" at upper right, "Isocitrate" at right upper-middle, "α-Ketoglutarate" at right lower-middle, "Succinyl-CoA" at bottom right, "Succinate" at bottom left, "Fumarate" at left lower-middle, and "Malate" at left upper-middle. Use readable 18-pixel-equivalent navy labels on opaque cream panels, with the longest name wrapped across two lines without changing its spelling. An entry arrow labeled "Acetyl-CoA" leads into the oxaloacetate-to-citrate reaction. A small outgoing "CoA-SH" tab sits beside that entry. At the isocitrate-to-alpha-ketoglutarate reaction, outgoing tags read "CO₂" and "NADH". At the alpha-ketoglutarate-to-succinyl-CoA reaction, outgoing tags again read "CO₂" and "NADH". At the succinyl-CoA-to-succinate reaction, outgoing tags read "CoA-SH" and "GTP → ATP". At the succinate-to-fumarate reaction, a tag reads "FADH₂"; place a small plain blue membrane-contact marker beside this reaction without lettering it. At the malate-to-oxaloacetate reaction, a tag reads "NADH". All product tags have navy lettering and pale blue backing. Leave generous spacing between tags and panels. No atom identities, extra words, reaction numbers, legend, or decorative lettering. This is the complete layout master; the animation will hide labels until their corresponding reaction occurs.

items.prompt:
Simple clean 2D animation, no music. Use the diagram layout of @cycle exactly, hiding labels until their beats. One fixed 16:9 view shows the peach mitochondrial cutaway, cream matrix and clockwise navy loop. Title is 28px navy; all other labels are 18px navy on cream or pale-blue backing, held after appearing. Product tags stay beside their reaction arrows. A calm adult English narrator speaks slowly and clearly; otherwise silence.
0–3 s: Reveal only the title 'Citric acid cycle' at top center; hold it still through the entire piece.
3–8 s: Reveal the loop inside the cutaway and 'Oxaloacetate' at upper left. The narrator says exactly: 'The Krebs cycle runs in the mitochondrial matrix.'
8–16 s: 'Acetyl-CoA' enters from above left. Its acetyl portion joins oxaloacetate; a separate 'CoA-SH' tab leaves. Reveal 'Citrate' at upper right. The narrator says exactly: 'Acetyl-CoA supplies two carbons, joining four-carbon oxaloacetate to form six-carbon citrate. Coenzyme A leaves.'
16–20 s: A clockwise pulse reaches 'Isocitrate' on the right. The narrator says exactly: 'Citrate rearranges into isocitrate.'
20–25 s: Reveal 'α-Ketoglutarate'; one 'CO₂' tag exits and one 'NADH' tag appears. The narrator says exactly: 'Carbon dioxide leaves, producing NADH and alpha-ketoglutarate.'
25–30 s: Reveal 'Succinyl-CoA' at bottom right; a second 'CO₂' exits and second 'NADH' appears. The narrator says exactly: 'Another carbon dioxide leaves, producing NADH and succinyl-CoA.' Do not trace incoming acetyl carbons into departing CO₂. No other text, cuts, music or subtitles.

Continue directly from @previous: the same scene, style, people and objects, mid-action. Simple clean 2D animation, no music. Keep @cycle's layout exactly: fixed 16:9 peach mitochondrial cutaway, cream matrix, navy clockwise loop. Preserve every visible label, including the still top title 'Citric acid cycle'. New labels use the same 18px navy lettering on cream or pale-blue backing and remain through the end. The narrator continues.
0–9 s: Continue the pulse from 'Succinyl-CoA' toward bottom-left 'Succinate'. A 'CoA-SH' tab leaves; beside the reaction reveal 'GTP → ATP', with a single energy token moving from GTP to ATP, not two products. The narrator says exactly: 'Succinyl-CoA becomes succinate, releasing coenzyme A. Energy is captured as GTP, then transferred to ATP.'
9–14 s: Pulse toward left-side 'Fumarate'; reveal one 'FADH₂' tag at the small membrane-contact marker. The narrator says exactly: 'Succinate becomes fumarate, producing FADH2.'
14–18 s: One small blue water droplet enters the arrow leading to 'Malate' above. The narrator says exactly: 'Water converts fumarate to malate.'
18–23 s: Pulse reaches the existing 'Oxaloacetate' panel; reveal the third 'NADH' tag beside this arrow. The narrator says exactly: 'Malate produces NADH, regenerating oxaloacetate.'
23–30 s: Close the highlighted loop. Another 'Acetyl-CoA' tab approaches the regenerated oxaloacetate and begins joining it; keep the complete diagram visible. The narrator says exactly: 'Oxaloacetate accepts another acetyl group, and the cycle starts again.' No other text, cuts, music or subtitles.
